purpose: Distinguish gain evolution during a silent prefix from an onset triggered by active samples. This does not certify arbitrary first-play behavior.

runs.priorPlaybackHistory: Last fixture played in prior turn; selected after silence-prefix trial

runs.sequence: Warmup selected with only the canonical reference manually queued; same exclusive connection remains armed across both
runs.comparator: Only canonical non-silent reference; warmup contributes silent margin, never an accepted reference by itself
runs.extraVariables: Queued continuous transition plus source-renderer activation; this is an exploratory composite prewarm condition, not isolated attribution.

commonConditions.routePreparation: Each CLI trial changes and restores the output route independently

hypotheses: If the newly selected silence-prefix file preserves all active samples, the captured startup transformation need not affect the later active portion under these conditions.
If rejection begins with the same gain-onset model at active sample zero, the onset may be tied to active playback rather than elapsed file silence.
The fitted recurrence alone does not reach exact unity when extended indefinitely in Float32, so a pass would require behavior outside the measured first512-frame model.
limits: Not randomized; prior player and route history are uncontrolled.
Silent source-frame duration cannot be distinguished from additional capture margin using samples alone.
A silent-prefix pass is not a repair or proof for arbitrary non-silent openings.
